title: Immune Complex Small Vessel Vasculitis and Behçet Disease

steps.tx: Immune complex-mediated small vessel vasculitides develop when circulating antigen-antibody complexes deposit in postcapillary venules, activating the classical complement cascade and recruiting neutrophils. Neutrophilic karyorrhexis with vascular wall necrosis produces the pathognomonic clinical hallmark termed **palpable purpura**, characterised by non-blanching raised erythematous lesions distributed symmetrically across dependent lower extremities.
steps.say: Immune complex-mediated small vessel vasculitides occur when antigen-antibody complexes deposit in postcapillary venules, activating complement and recruiting neutrophils. Neutrophil nuclear fragmentation produces the classic sign termed palpable purpura, presenting as non-blanching raised lesions across dependent lower extremities.

steps.tx: The most common systemic vasculitis of childhood is an IgA-dominant immune complex vasculitis historically termed **Henoch-Schönlein purpura** (HSP, now classified as IgA vasculitis). Triggered frequently by an antecedent upper respiratory tract infection, HSP manifests as a classic tetrad of palpable cutaneous purpura, periarticular non-deforming arthralgias, colicky abdominal pain, and glomerulonephritis.

steps.tx: Histopathology of skin lesions in IgA vasculitis shows leukocytoclastic vasculitis of postcapillary venules with perivascular neutrophilic dust. Direct immunofluorescence of dermal and renal biopsies demonstrates predominant granular vascular deposition of **immunoglobulin A** (specifically galactose-deficient IgA1) and complement C3 within capillary walls and glomerular mesangium, identical to the renal lesions of primary IgA nephropathy.

Direct immunofluorescence of dermal and renal biopsies demonstrates predominant granular vascular deposition of immunoglobulin A and complement C3 within capillary walls and glomerular mesangium.

steps.tx: Cold-precipitable circulating immunoglobulins characterise another distinct immune complex small vessel vasculitis designated as **cryoglobulinaemic vasculitis**. Type II and III mixed cryoglobulinaemias contain monoclonal or polyclonal IgM rheumatoid factor bound to polyclonal IgG, strongly associated in over eighty percent of instances with chronic hepatitis C virus infection.
steps.say: Cold-precipitable circulating immunoglobulins characterize another distinct immune complex small vessel vasculitis designated as cryoglobulinaemic vasculitis. Mixed cryoglobulinaemia involves monoclonal or polyclonal IgM rheumatoid factor bound to IgG, strongly associated with chronic hepatitis C virus infection.

steps.tx: A multi-system, chronic relapsing inflammatory disorder capable of involving vessels of all sizes across both arterial and venous systems is **Behçet disease**. It exhibits a distinctive geographic distribution concentrated along the ancient Silk Road, spanning the Mediterranean basin, Middle East, and East Asia, and displays a strong genetic association with HLA-B51.

It exhibits a distinctive geographic distribution concentrated along the ancient Silk Road and displays a strong genetic association with human leukocyte antigen B51.

steps.tx: The pathognomonic hallmark of Behçet disease is the recurrent development of painful oral aphthae occurring at least three times over a twelve-month interval. These are accompanied by painful scarring **genital ulcers** affecting the scrotum or vulva, relapsing non-granulomatous hypopyon panuveitis threatening vision, and spontaneous deep vein thromboses or pulmonary arterial pseudoaneurysms.
steps.say: The clinical hallmark of Behçet disease is the recurrent development of painful oral aphthae occurring at least three times yearly. These are accompanied by painful genital ulcers on the scrotum or vulva, relapsing hypopyon panuveitis threatening sight, and spontaneous venous or arterial thromboses.

steps.tx: A highly specific physical finding reflecting non-specific cutaneous neutrophil hyperreactivity to minor mechanical trauma is the **pathergy test**. Following oblique intradermal puncture of the forearm with a sterile twenty-gauge needle, the appearance of an erythematous sterile papule or pustule measuring two millimetres or larger within twenty-four to forty-eight hours confirms a positive diagnostic response.
steps.say: A highly specific diagnostic finding reflecting cutaneous neutrophil hyperreactivity to minor mechanical trauma is the pathergy test. Following intradermal puncture of the forearm with a sterile needle, development of an erythematous sterile papule or pustule within forty-eight hours confirms a positive result.

steps.tx: Therapeutic strategies in immune complex vasculitis focus on the underlying trigger and organ involvement. Pediatric IgA vasculitis is typically self-limiting and managed with supportive hydration and analgesia, reserving corticosteroids for severe abdominal pain or crescentic nephritis. Cryoglobulinaemic vasculitis requires antiviral eradication of hepatitis C using direct-acting antivirals, while Behçet disease responds to **colchicine** for mucocutaneous lesions and azathioprine or anti-TNF agents for ocular and vascular disease.
steps.say: Therapeutic strategies in immune complex vasculitides focus on the underlying trigger and organ involvement. Pediatric IgA vasculitis is typically self-limiting and managed supportively. Cryoglobulinaemic vasculitis requires direct-acting antivirals for hepatitis C, while Behçet disease responds to colchicine for mucosal ulcers and anti-TNF therapies for severe ocular involvement.
